data.title: Plan-system rollout — master
data.phase: active · S3 in flight · plans-infra next
data.summary: Master plan tracking the end-to-end roll-out of the plan-system redesign. Owns the S3 sprint, the open decisions that apply across the rollout, and the bootstrap principle: use the new infrastructure to ship itself.

sections.body: The plan-system redesign (prototype delivered 2026-05-21) is shipping in waves. dotfiles canonical landed at 7530860; ambix system pages landed at 3d3df82; tight-loop POST + identity fix + hide-shipped landed at 209b14c; live-fetch cutover landed at c1d9cf4 + c4a7ebe + 6137f4b; MOCK→STATE rename landed at 067aa94. This master plan owns the remaining waves and the open decisions that span them.

Five items in S3: plans-infra (skill + state.js + plan-init), plans-agile-sprints (sprint flow with agent input), plans-migration-ambix (12 per-plan pages), plans-migration-efit (8 top-level + 51 curated/), and this master. Bootstrap-priority decision locked 2026-05-21 12:49 to serial order (Infra → Agile → Ambix → Efit). plans-infra begins next.

S3 lives inside the very system it builds. Every decision we make about the design is captured as an inline-decision row on the relevant plan. Every handoff between sessions is a followup with the §05 prompt template. The act of running S3 is itself the integration test — verified on 2026-05-21 when typing 'rationale' on bootstrap-priority wrote through to docs/state/imas-ambix/plans-redesign-rollout.json (integration test passed, see f-prio-1).

S3 closes when (a) plan-infra has POSTing state.js + extended plan-style + new plan-init; (b) plans-agile-sprints has a locked cadence + agent-rationale model; (c) plans-migration-ambix has at least one redesigned per-plan page approved and the pattern proven; (d) plans-migration-efit has CSS migrated + plan-test demoed; (e) this master has resolved its open decisions and locked the bootstrap order (DONE).

decisions_def.title: Bootstrap ordering — what ships first within S3?
decisions_def.context: Five items in S3. They're not strictly serial — infra unblocks everything, but migration could start in parallel with reduced scope. Order shapes what the user sees first.
choices: Infra → Agile → Ambix migration → Efit migration (serial, dependency order)
Infra parallel with Ambix-migration-pilot; agile last (parallel where possible)
Migration first (visible UX); infra second; agile last

bootstrap-priority.choice: Infra → Agile → Ambix migration → Efit migration (serial, dependency order)

notes.body: Created via /plan-create with the user's instruction to bootstrap. We use this very plan-page to track the rollout — the decisions on this page WILL be tested as feedback-loop drivers.

Integration test verified end-to-end (f-prio-1 resolved). bootstrap-priority locked to serial order. plans-infra has 2/3 decisions locked (conflict-detection=version+412, rank-storage=sibling rank.json); shared-css-delivery is pending user weigh-in on CDN explanation. Implementation of plans-infra begins now with the two locked constraints honoured; CSS-delivery flow stays manual /plan-style refresh until the third decision lands.

followups.title: Implement plans-infra: state.js POST + plan-style sync + plan-init skill
followups.body: Bootstrap-priority is locked to serial order; plans-infra is next. Two of three plans-infra decisions are locked: conflict-detection=version+412 (state JSON gains a version integer; POST sends expected version; server returns 412 on mismatch), rank-storage=sibling rank.json (separate file, not embedded). shared-css-delivery is unresolved (CDN explanation pending); ship with manual /plan-style refresh as the default behaviour until that decision lands.
followups.prompt:
Project: dotfiles + imas-ambix
Plan:    plans-infra
Section: § 2 + § 3 + § 4
Tier:    opus (coordinator) + sonnet (workers)

Context
  Three connected dotfiles changes. The plans-infra plan documents the
  scope; two of its three decisions are locked.

State to read
  docs/state/imas-ambix/plans-infra.json   (decisions + locked constraints)
  ~/Code/dotfiles/claude/skills/html-docs/assets/state.js
  ~/Code/dotfiles/claude/skills/html-docs/templates/ui.jsx  (Persist already POSTs)
  ~/Code/dotfiles/docs-server/serve.py
  ~/Code/dotfiles/claude/skills/plan-style/SKILL.md

Locked decisions to honour
  conflict-detection → version field + 412 on mismatch
    – state JSON gains data._version (integer, starts at 1)
    – Persist.save() / state.js saveState() send {expected_version: N} in POST
    – serve.py returns 412 when state file's _version != expected_version
    – Client on 412: re-fetch, replay patch, retry POST once; otherwise surface conflict
  rank-storage → sibling rank.json
    – state/<project>/rank.json holds {<slug>: <int>, …}
    – inventory ordering reads rank.json first, falls back to existing sort keys
  ship-via-pages, prompt-template, state-promotion, model-tier-naming
    – per /home/ITER/mcintos/.agents/AGENTS.md

Open decisions to surface (do not resolve)
  shared-css-delivery (waiting on user)

Constraints
  - Schema changes are additive. Existing state JSON without _version reads as version 0.
  - state.js POST has localStorage fallback when docs-server unreachable.
  - plan-style refresh syncs the SYSTEM pages (project.html→index.html, inventory.html,
    sprint.html, decisions.html, plan.html, ui.jsx, state-loader.js, foundation.css,
    dashboard.css, project.css) from dotfiles canonical to <repo>/docs/. Idempotent.
  - plan-init creates a NEW repo's docs/ from scratch. Repo-agnostic.

Done-when
  1. state.js POSTs to docs-server in local mode with version header; localStorage fallback.
  2. ui.jsx Persist.save() also sends version (parity with state.js).
  3. serve.py rejects POST with 412 on version mismatch.
  4. /plan-style refresh syncs system pages + CSS + state-loader.js + ui.jsx.
  5. /plan-init exists at ~/.claude/skills/plan-init/ + claude/commands/plan-init.md.
  6. All three documented in their SKILL.md.
  7. Followup written outlining the next sprint item (plans-agile-sprints OR migration pilot).

followups.outcome: Feedback loop verified end-to-end. User typed rationale='rationale' on bootstrap-priority (2026-05-21 12:25, by 'Simon McIntosh') — POST wrote through to docs/state/imas-ambix/plans-redesign-rollout.json. Subsequently user locked the choice to 'Infra → Agile → Ambix migration → Efit migration' (2026-05-21 12:49). Both writes preserved through the Path-A live-fetch cutover (commits c1d9cf4 + c4a7ebe + 6137f4b) and the MOCK→STATE rename (067aa94). Page UI confirmed via curl on https://simon-mcintosh.github.io/imas-ambix/state/imas-ambix/plans-redesign-rollout.json. The loop is closed.

followups.body: The tight-loop POST is wired (Persist.save in ui.jsx POSTs to docs-server). Visit the local URL, click bootstrap-priority chips + type rationale, hit Send. We expect docs/state/imas-ambix/plans-redesign-rollout.json to appear and contain the locked decision. This is the integration test for the whole feedback loop.
followups.prompt:
Project: imas-ambix
Plan:    plans-redesign-rollout
Section: § decisions · bootstrap-priority
Tier:    haiku (verify-only)

Context
  This followup is the first integration test of the tight-loop POST.
  Open http://localhost:8765/imas-ambix/plan.html?slug=plans-redesign-rollout
  on the local docs-server (with tunnel up), click one of the
  bootstrap-priority chips, type a one-line rationale, hit Send/Enter.

State to read
  docs/state/imas-ambix/plans-redesign-rollout.json  (will be created on first POST)

Locked decisions to honour (none yet on this plan)

Open decisions to surface
  bootstrap-priority (this is the one being tested)

Done-when

  2. The page UI shows the chosen chip + the typed rationale on reload.
  3. Mark this followup resolved with outcome 'feedback loop verified'.
  4. Write the next followup: which item in S3 to start on (infra vs migration-pilot vs agile).
